The objective wording is the course seed's. (read for this round by an earlier pass on 2026-11-17)

Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: 'ExpressRoute supports up to 4,000 IPv4 prefixes ... advertised to Microsoft through the Azure private peering' (10,000 with the premium add-on); 'The BGP session drops if the number of prefixes exceeds the limit'; advertising a default route into private peering 'block[s] the internet path from Azure' and 'breaks Windows and other VM license activation'. The page does not say when the session comes back after the count is reduced; that it re-establishes once the edge stops exceeding the limit, and the az CLI output, are from memory (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the network engineer at Lindqvist Foods. The data centers reach the Azure hub over an ExpressRoute circuit (Standard, private peering). At 09:40 the on-premises team turned on redistribution of their whole internal routing table into BGP toward Azure 'so every branch is reachable'. Since then Azure VMs cannot reach any on-premises network. The 11:00 production planning run reads the on-premises MES from Azure.
handover: The on-premises edge routers are run by the data center network team; their change window is still open.
Before 09:40 the edge advertised 14 summary prefixes.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the on-premises edge, the circuit's private peering sessions and the routes Azure learns.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the sessions kept dropping, what was changed and by whom, and how it is prevented.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: At 09:40 the edge redistributed the internal table and advertised 4,350 prefixes; a Standard circuit's private peering accepts 4,000, so the session closed (the edge logged MAXPFX) and Azure learned nothing.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: With the DC network team the redistribution was rolled back and a prefix list advertises the 14 summaries again; both sessions are stable. A default route would have hijacked Azure's internet path; resetting the peering only repeated the drop.

parts.label: Prevented
parts.modelAnswer: A maximum-prefix warning at 3,000 on the edges, a written advertisement standard, and an alert on BGP availability.

scoring.modelReasoning: Azure learns no on-premises routes and the edge logs a maximum-prefix close: redistribution pushed 4,350 prefixes over a Standard circuit's 4,000 limit, so the session drops. Have the edge go back to advertising its summaries, which already cover every branch, and the sessions stay up. A default route over private peering blocks Azure's internet path; a peering reset just drops again. Then warn on prefix count and alert on BGP availability.
